text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Retirement fund forecasts that a shift to early retirement at 55 years would cost some 120 billion francs and imply a seven-point rise of mandatory retirement contributions.
-- Societe Generale chairman Marc Vienot says does not rule out seizing other growth opportunities after buying Credit du Nord, seeks to maintain a 10 percent profit ratio on invested funds.
-- Thomson Multimedia is expected to post a 3-billion-franc loss for 1996 including a 500 million operating losses.

-- National Assembly Finance Committee denies approval to creation of an investigation committee to look into the Credit Foncier accounts. Finance Minister Jean Arthuis calls for a quick implementation of a bailout plan involving a partial transfer of loan activity and staff to Credit Immobilier de France.
-- Government to decide on the terms of sale for Thomson-CSF before the end of the month.
-- A buyout offer on media group CEP being prepared by Havas is to be a first step of a wider restructuring at Havas.
-- The state and Dassault near agreement on the purchase of 48 Rafale fighter aircraft.
-- French military procurement agency is seeking price cuts in exchange for orders, according to spokeswoman at defense electronics firm Thomson-CSF.
-- France Telecom competitors who will enter the French market in 1998 may obtain lower interconnection charges than initially announced by the state-owned operator.
